chapter: Buddy Petit, Kid Thomas and working life
title: Buddy Petit's style, band and drummer Sammy Penn
summary: Buddy played a six-piece band, soft, not a high-note man, and harmonized under Burbank's lead; Penn and George Washington played drums.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah. How many trumpet players does Buddy have in his band? Himself. No other? No other. It's a six piece band. Is anybody around that plays anything like Buddy? Sometimes he can count himself. Anybody around that plays anything like Buddy? No.
I don't know anybody that plays anything like Buddy. What kind of a style did he have? Was he loud?

He wasn't so loud and he wasn't a high note man. He made so much in the race and stuff. Would he play lead all the time? No. He'd get all. He'd get all. Would you ever carry the lead with him very long? He'd make a lot of chords. Would he play back to you when you had the lead or not? Sometime. What kind of a part would he play there? Would he play some? He'd make a second. Make a second to you. Second drumming part.
You would play the melody, he'd make a second.

Who else was in that band? I see. Samuel Penn was playing drum. George Washington was playing drum. I don't remember. I just can't remember the other voice. What about Sammy Penn in those days? Did he play as loud as he does now? Yeah. He's plenty loud now. Did he make a lot of explosions and stuff then or was he more of a straight drum or what? He's played very much like he's playing now. But I think he's more improved now. I see.
You like to work with him? Oh yeah.
